subject: PulseHealth: pulse credit top-up, inline billing path & synchronization
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pulsehealth.ai>

Cc: procurement@pulsehealth.ai

Subject: Unexpected Q4 surge — looking for short-term top-up + alignment

Hi Chloe / Ben,

Quick note from our side — we had a larger-than-expected pilot launch this week and are tracking ~2.8x our forecast for the month. We expect sustained elevated inference usage through the end of the quarter.

Can Redwood provide a short-term top-up of capacity and a one-off credit to smooth billing? Ideally we would:
- Add a 30% capacity top-up for December (true-up billed in January)
- Receive a one-time 10% credit on the top-up portion given the sudden nature of this (customer goodwill ask)
- Consider aligning our contract to the calendar year so future renewals are simpler (we're currently mid-cycle).

I've looped in procurement — they may request paperwork. Need a quick sketch/quote and confirmation of what you can do this week.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director of Product, PulseHealth
liam.oconnor@pulsehealth.ai

Date: 2027-12-11T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Q4 surge — looking for short-term top-up + alignment

Hi Liam — appreciate the heads up and congrats on the pilot lift. Short answers: yes, we can support an interim top-up and we have two pragmatic paths for billing/term alignment.

Attached: pulse_quote_v3.pdf (sketch pricing for a 30% top-up + two credit scenarios). Also included a draft SOW for operational handoff.

Options (summary):
1) Short-term top-up (recommended):
   - 30% capacity add for Dec (billed pro-rata on next invoice).
   - Option A: one-time 10% goodwill credit applied to the top-up invoice (limited to this incident).
   - Option B: 5% credit now + priority access to burst buffer for January as non-monetary concession.

2) Co-term / sync into calendar year (longer process):
   - We can annualize the remainder of your current term and align to calendar year on renewal; this requires a short amendment and will pro-rate remaining months.

Next steps I propose: Ben to confirm pricing breakouts on attached; procurement to confirm PO window; we schedule a 30-min triage for tomorrow to lock option.

If that works I can standby with a signed amendment template to expedite.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Liam / Chloe — quick pricing clarity from my side. I ran numbers across the current commit and a 30% top-up:

- Baseline unit price: $0.0026 / token-equivalent (existing commit).
- Top-up (30% extra capacity for remainder of Dec): billed at baseline * 1.15 (short-term premium) => $0.00299 / token-eq.
- One-time credit scenarios:
   • 10% credit applied to top-up invoice => net top-up rate ≈ $0.00269 / token-eq for the top-up portion.
   • 5% credit + priority burst in Jan => effectively $0.00284 / token-eq + operational buffer.

If procurement needs an invoice now I can prepare a pro-forma by EOD. For co-terming (sync to calendar): I recommend annualizing rather than shortening — this minimizes churn in unit economics and lets us preserve the committed discount. I included two amortization options in pulse_quote_v3.pdf.

Ben

Thanks all — a few operational and billing notes from finance:

- We can issue the pro-forma for the pro-rata top-up immediately; it will be invoiced on your next monthly invoice (Jan) as a line item labeled "Dec top-up — PulseHealth".
- Credits: we can apply a one-time credit to the invoice, but credits require sign-off if >$25k. Please flag if top-up expected to exceed that.
- Co-term amendment: if you choose annualization, we'll send an amendment that outlines the pro-rata charge and a clear start/end date. That amendment will require a countersigned PO/DocuSign.

Operational ask: Liam, can you confirm expected delta in peak RPS and whether you want the top-up to be strictly capacity units or a combination of capacity + burst buffer? That changes the tech-side provisioning timeline (capacity-only is faster).

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Billing Manager, Redwood Inference
